The strip down the chosen colour card, in grey instead of pink.

S1 with your changes: the highlighted folder wears today's white bar and only it shows its path; the rest are a name each. The last row says "type the path here · or drop a folder". "type to rename" is gone. What varies: how the name says it can be changed, and how "name" and "to" are emphasised. Each shows the list at rest, then a path being typed.

The tabs are now formats on the mode's tint, and the format is gone from inside the before panel, since its tab says it. The hatching is a tint and three rows tall, beside the panel only. Three questions, one row each: what the after tab says, the arrow, and whether the panels share a fill.

Why light looks flat today, and a proposal. Greys: light still uses the warm beige greys dark gave up on 11 October; swapped for pure greys of the same lightness, as dark's were. Gradients: dark's stops are light, saturated colours (OKLCH lightness ≈ 0.75) — on white most fall to 1.5–2.5:1 and wash out, which is why light uses a separate, duller set. A colour "pops" on white when it is mid-light with as much chroma as the screen can show: so each of dark's stops keeps its hue, takes the most chroma sRGB allows, and is darkened until it reaches 4.5:1 on white, which keeps it above WCAG's 3:1 for graphics (SC 1.4.11) on the grey panel too, where the dots sit. (A first try at 3.4:1 looked brighter in the table but fell to 2.7:1 on the panel: paler, not punchier.) Convert and compress barely change — today's teal and green are already near the edge of what the screen can show at that lightness; the gains are in colour, enhance and pdf. Colour mode gets its spectrum back, and enhance gets a real gradient instead of two near-identical violets. Text colours are unchanged: they already clear 4.5:1.
